clue.text: Witty exchanges about golfing terms

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
par is a golfing term: the standard score for a hole
tee is a golfing term: the peg or spot from which a hole starts

explanation.surface: Golfers trading banter in the jargon of their game.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-witted banter traded back and forth between speakers is what this word names.

clue.text: Beam and post at bottom of river

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: A timber and a stake lying on a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the sloping timbers supporting a roof is a beam of this kind.

clue.text: Chum to make the attempt? It's not worth serious consideration

parts.note: a pal is a chum
to try is to make the attempt

explanation.surface: A friend's half-hearted effort is dismissed as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling or meagre, too small an amount to matter.

clue.text: Bird on its perch?

parts.note: a bird settled on its perch for the night could be called one that roosts

explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a farmyard bird, and the word also suggests one who settles to sleep on a perch.

clue.text: Seek sport supplements

indicators.note: to sport letters is to play with them, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hunting for sports nutrition products.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke out is to make something go further by adding to it.

clue.text: Creature seen from one in boat going round the point

indicators.note: the boat goes round the compass point and the one, holding both inside it

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
E, east, is a point of the compass
A is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone in a boat rounding a headland spots a marine animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' has the boat enclose the point followed by the one; a sea cow is a manatee or dugong, not something seen on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugong or manatee, a large plant-eating marine mammal, is called by this name.

clue.text: Give the subject a title

parts.note: sounds like heading an essay, but means the monarch making one of her subjects a lord

explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage, making them a lord or lady.

clue.text: Camping out in a military operation

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers bivouacking during manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised series of military actions with one objective.

clue.text: In stampede, damaged shawl I'd wrapped round daughter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are wrapped round the daughter, holding her inside
the letters are damaged, so broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: In a crush, a torn shawl is wrapped round a girl to protect her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' is the anagram signal and 'wrapped round' the container; the newspaper scan reads 'shaw!', an OCR slip for 'shawl', which the letter count requires.
explanation.definitionFit: A frantic headlong rush, like a herd charging in panic.

clue.text: Hawker with no wares to sell

definitions.text: Hawker with no wares to sell

parts.words: Hawker with no wares to sell
parts.note: a hawker normally peddles goods, but here it is someone who keeps and flies hawks

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trains and hunts with hawks is literally a hawker, though he sells nothing.

clue.text: Beastly article received by mail order

indicators.note: the article is taken in at the front of the rearranged letters, standing ahead of them

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: putting the letters of mail in a new order shuffles them

explanation.surface: Something nasty arrives through a mail-order catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks part of the phrase mail order, but it is the anagram signal; 'received by' simply sets the article in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means bodily, brutish or bestial, like beastly.

clue.text: Break up — cast off better half

indicators.note: off signals the letters are thrown off their order and rearranged
only half of better is used, its second half

explanation.surface: A divorce: throwing out one's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CAST to SCAT; 'half' keeps TER from BETTER. A 'better half' is a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse or send things flying in different directions.

clue.text: Birds for example disturbed rest

indicators.note: the letters of rest are disturbed, so shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Some birds, perhaps, have their rest disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are white herons, a family of wading birds.

clue.text: The case of the black-leg poet

parts.note: a blackleg or scab is a strike-breaker
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A mystery about a poet who crossed a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath for a sword or dagger is the case it is kept in.

clue.text: Keep an eye on position of bishop

definitions.meaning: a bishop is set over his see, the diocese he governs

explanation.definitionFit: Supervise; and, read as two words, above a diocese, where a bishop stands in authority.

clue.text: Stretches of greenery thrips have half demolished, in border

indicators.note: the border is taken in among the rearranged letters
the letters are knocked down and rebuilt in a new arrangement
only half of the word have is used, its second half

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Tiny insects have ravaged the shrubbery along a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the back half of have; 'demolished' shuffles that with thrips (tiny plant-eating insects), and the border goes in just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is a common evergreen shrub planted in rows as boundary greenery in British gardens.

clue.text: Fateful mix-up in opening number making one flush

indicators.note: the jumbled letters open up to take the number inside
the letters of the word are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A lucky number turns out to make someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' turns FATEFUL into AFFLUET, which opens to take N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of money, wealthy.

clue.text: Refuse to go below

definitions.meaning: to reject an offer or request
a bend in a road or path that heads downhill

explanation.definitionFit: Decline or reject; and, as two words, a bend leading lower down.

clue.text: Apocalyptic group of riders

parts.note: the Book of Revelation (the Apocalypse) describes a band of riders bringing conquest, war, famine and death

explanation.definitionFit: Revelation names a quartet of mounted figures who herald the end of the world.

clue.text: As a last resort calls for money

definitions.text: As a last resort calls for money

parts.words: As a last resort calls for money
parts.note: a last resort here is a final place of care for the dying, a charity which appeals for funds

explanation.definitionFit: A home caring for the terminally ill, often run as a charity.

clue.text: In the Mid-West a mistake gets past

indicators.note: the mistake is put in the middle letters
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the American Midwest a blunder slips by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mid-West' suggests America, but 'Mid-' just takes the centre of the word West; 'In' sets the mistake inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by or goes on.

clue.text: Fit a particular environment and live to a great age?

definitions.meaning: to be at home in a place or group
read as two words, to exist for a long time

explanation.definitionFit: Fit in naturally somewhere; and, split, to last a lengthy lifetime.

clue.text: King George, specifically a rider, takes it in

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
as introduces a specific role, as in acting as chair
a PS, a postscript, is a rider added to a letter

explanation.surface: A monarch, as a horseman, takes in the view.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand something fully, to comprehend it.

clue.text: Painter, late starter then prophet

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: and can mean then, as in one thing and another
a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: An artist who got going late in life, then turned visionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals, who also designed the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Landseer was a celebrated nineteenth-century English artist.

clue.text: Tend to pause, in headlong rush

parts.note: to care for something is to tend it; care here stands for tending
er is the sound of a hesitating pause in speech

explanation.surface: Advice to stop and look after things in the middle of a mad dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle along at great speed, so the noun is a wild onward rush.

clue.text: Piano tune suitable for a duet

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A piece of piano music written for two players.
explanation.definitionFit: Two together form a couple or duo, as a duet's performers do.

clue.text: Boy is holding book — a sex manual?

indicators.note: the boy holds the book inside his name

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
OT, the Old Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A lad caught clutching a racy book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a sex manual is something sexual in nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arousing or concerned with sexual desire, as such a guide would be.

clue.text: Strong feelings caused by transfer charges

parts.note: to pass something is to transfer it
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: Tempers flare over transfer fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense emotions such as love, rage or desire.

clue.text: Metal turned colour — it's highly combustible

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: the colour is turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A metal changes colour as it burns fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry material used for lighting fires catches flame very easily.

clue.text: Forecasts appearing in the papers — about time!

indicators.note: the papers go about, surrounding, the time

parts.note: the press means the newspapers
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Predictions in the newspapers, long overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell or be a sign of something to come, as omens do.
